What is
MARGO - On the Brink
?
MARGO - On the Brink
is a turn-based 2D RPG with roguelites deck-builder elements. You play as
a nameless girl, [Null],
trapped in a crumbling reality known as the Brink, a world filled with broken and useless things. As her life slowly fades,
[Null]
must find a way to recover and escape the Brink.
However, the Junkyard is patrolled by malevolent entities called the
Watchers
. They are determined to destroy
[Null]
, whom they see as "The Pretender" and the greatest threat to their world.
[Null]
must form unbreakable bonds with benevolent beings known as the
Whispers
and connect them to a primordial energy know as the Source, empowering them to stand against the Watchers' tyranny.
What are the main characters like?
We strive to make every character you meet in
MARGO
distinct and memorable, except for the main character, [Null], who is your typical JRPG silent protagonist. Instead of introducing the characters through posts, we want players to meet them in the game and let the story unfold naturally.
We hope these characters stay with you long after you finish the game.
Gameplay?
MARGO
is a slow-paced, turn-based RPG where strategic decisions are key to mastering the game. As a roguelite deck-builder, you must utilize every random card you have to win battles. Even a single wrong move can end a run.
When defeated in combat, you lose all collected cards and dungeon progress. However, the levels of the Whispers and their cards are retained, allowing you to start the next run a bit stronger. There’s no unnecessary grinding, as enemies do not respawn unless the run resets, and there are no random encounters.
Combat Showcase
Side Quests?
We apply the same design philosophy to our game's side quests as we do to our characters. We want them to stay with you long after you've completed the game. There will be no fetch quests or "kill X number of enemies" quests. There are no side quest markers or quest logs. Instead, we want players to discover side quests organically for a more rewarding experience.

posts.author: SomaelCK
posts.body:
Hello folks! It has been a long time since we last update about our project! (Exactly 1 year!). Due to unforeseen circumstances and political unrest in my country, we had to halt the project for several months.
The good thing is, we are back on track now and we've several major update for our project!
First of all, here is the new 4K artwork for the game.
This will be our main promotional art. Let's know what you think about this.
Gameplay Loop
MARGO will be a grind-free turn-based RPG with soft-core roguelite/card-battle elements. The game will featured 5 main dungeons with 1 DLC dungeon planned. Player can gain new skills and upgrades as random cards in dungeons.
They have to make use of the randomness to their advantage to conquer the challenges in the dungeon. Quitting the dungeon without completing or getting a gameover will wipe the cards/skill in your hands and you will have to start from the square one again. However, the progress will be saved once you cleared a dungeon. You don't have to start over from first dungeon again, even if you failed in the second dungeon.
As you progress, you will gain permanent currency that could be used to directly manipulate the odds in your favor. The more you play, the luckier you will be.
More friends, more power!
You draw power from the mysterious entities called the "Whispers". Once you unlocked a Whisper, new cards and skills related to it will start to drop in dungeon. They will get stronger as you progress and you will have more cards and skills to use in battles. Strategically plan and use them in battles to chain the combos and turn the tides in your favor!
Gameplay Footage
Have a look at pre-alpha game-play of MARGO sans the battle system. We are hoping to release a playable demo soon!
That's all for now! Let me know what you think about our game and its gameplay loop.
Cheers!

posts.author: SomaelCK
posts.body:
Hi folks!
Been a while since the last update! We've been working over our custom battle system and it's finally taking shape. Here is a quick run down!
Program Cards
These are the meat and bone of the entire battle system. MARGO has a (very light) roguelite progression system where you earn random program cards (skills) in dungeon related to the
Lost Whispers
you earned (These cute creatures)
As there are no random encounter and the program cards you can hold is limited, the main challenge of the game will be the resource management based on the RNG. We plan to add about 100 program cards for you to collect and use in the combat.
Some rare cards may unleash a powerful summoning attack like this:
Things can get dicey
Regardless of which program card you choose, Null and Lumi will attack the enemy by default, after you selected the "Execute" command. This attack is entirely depended on dice rolls. Lumi started with the attack power of 1D6. This can be improved later in the game.
Battle Gameplay
That's a wrap for now. Thanks for reading this long post! Comments on what you see so far would be really helpful for us. Can't wait to show more about the game. Cheers!
Spoiler

posts.author: SomaelCK
posts.body:
Hi, I have some substantial updates for MARGO's gameplay!
Update for battle system
Enemies will have unique animations which you can use to determine what they are going to do. Reading the "tells" from the enemies will be crucial deciding factor between victory and defeat.
Smart Enemy AI [WIP]
Instead of attacking randomly, some enemies in MARGO will have "smart" AI that will try find the most effective solution to destroy the player. For example, you are low on heath and have a healing card in your hand, then enemy with "healing jammer" ability will try to nullify the healing or even try to corrupt the healing into DMG in later dungeons.
Mods -
... So on
Mods are the another crucial element player will need to make use in order to successfully complete a dungeon. In early game, they will be very basic buff, like adding +1 to healing or DMG etc but late game mods will have powerful unique buff and some debuff to balance the game.
They can't be swapped out or deleted once you pick them up. The only way to get rid of them is to die in the dungeon, which will wipe everything in roguelite fashion or find a mod removal machine in dungeon which will remove ALL of the attached mods for a fee.
Thanks for reading and have a nice day! Cheers!

posts.author: SomaelCK
posts.body:
I think MARGO - On the Brink's first showcase to general public in an event was a great success!
A lot of people waiting in que to play MARGO, till the end of the event! We set up two computers for demo play but both of them are filled all the time.We are the only ones who are showcasing an RPG Maker project in the event.
What's surprised me is that almost everyone one sat down and played the 30+ minutes demo to the end. Being an RPG, MARGO was quite text heavy and I thought people would drop it around midway. Instead we had players waiting in que til the end of the events. Some couldn't even play it due to long que.
Got a lot of feedback as well. Many enjoyed the story and game's aesthetic! Said it's very interesting so they want to see it through the end.
This event was a much needed confident booster for me! Will work on releasing the playable demo and get the game release on Early Access next.
We had an eager player as soon as the event started!
Lucky that we set up two computers!
A long wait que to test play MARGO.

posts.author: SomaelCK
posts.body:
Introducing two new Whispers;
Lapis
and
Jasper
What's unique about them is they are actually just one Whisper with two different split personalities. They transform between kind and mellow
Lapis
and rather feisty and brash
Jasper.
Gameplay-wise, their cards reflect this duality. Lapis cards transform into Jasper, and Jasper's into Lapis, and vice versa after the cards have been used. Jasper cards are offense-oriented, while Lapis cards focus on healing and buffs. Although these cards aren't as strong as specialized role-focused Whispers like Lullaby or Bulwark, their ability to switch between two different roles gives them an overall advantage in utility.
That's all. See you all in next update.
Cheers!

Oh, that's a data cache. By opening it, you gets cards which you can pick the card you'd like for your current hand (You can hold 5 cards in the begining).
Hack option is locked for now. It's basically "Magic" option in RPGs which the Main Character learned nothing yet, so can't be selected yet.
In battle, you have to select a card you want to use. Then press (Shift Key or Square/Y for controller) to prime/ready/comfirm the card selection. Then use "Execute" command and the primed card(s) will be used on selected target. MC auto attack the selected target regardless.
I know this one is a bit confusing lol since you have to confirm selected card with Shift key in install menu. The reason for that later part of the game, you can select up to 3 cards from your hand for card combos. So it's designed in a way where you make the card selection, the confirm with Shift button. The selected cards will be used when you pick execute command.
Sorry for the confusion! Maybe I should tutorialized this section better!

posts.author: RCXGaming
posts.body:
Hello,
@SomaelCK
! I wanted to cover MARGO because it looked extremely promising. The Feedback Festival helped push me to make this review, but trust me when I say I would have picked it out regardless due to the amount of work you put in to make the game look the way it does.
I had to stop an hour and 30 minutes into my playthrough - because if I didn’t, I genuinely would still be playing right now. Which is a big thing for me to say.
--
Spoiler:
MARGO Review
Spoiler:
Pros
+
Breathtaking title screen and music, especially with how it continues when you press New Game.
+
The game does not let up with how gorgeous it is, ranging from the expressive overworld sprites, full screen animated CGs and the full-bodied animated sprites for characters in combat. It is easily the best part of this game, and barring the little RPG Maker icons you’d probably never tell this was made in MV. Very good work.
+
I’m really digging this cybermaze aesthetic. Reminds me of Digimon.
+
I do like that for as much as the game is chock full of lore (EG. The Source, the fact these little computer faeries can be used as weapons and spells, etc.), the game doesn’t shove it down your throat for the entire experience. You’re kind of expected to piece it together yourself, which is far more preferable.
+
It helps that the actual writing helps make the characters very charming (like my boy Bulwark, what a chad + the shy computer that makes blushy faces at you)
+
Despite the fact our main character girl doesn’t speak, her sprites make her very emotive and that’s more than enough to win me over. In fact, there’s so many little touches (ex. Casting a shadow when against a door, sitting down on the ground to listen to the computer, etc.)
+
The save room where our little gal and the computer faeries are sitting resting on a bench is so adorable.
+
This has to be one of the most unique menus I’ve ever seen in RPG Maker. It’s so slick and cool-looking, especially the card stuff. However...
+
I do like that the enemies are patrolling the overworld so you’re not just ambushed by random encounters. Very nice.
+
This card gameplay is genuinely addicting. Like it’s luck-dependent due to being a roguelite deck-building game (read below for my issues with that), but it turns this otherwise simple battle system into something I can see people sinking tons of hours into.
Especially given how the effects of your little computer faeries activates immediately when you select them.
Running into those card caches gives me the same dopamine as gacha hunting, I’m not joking.
+
Oh interesting. The floors are randomized, since the floor I started on in my next attempt wasn't the same as the last time.
Spoiler:
Observations
=
The enemies say “Subjucation” in cutscenes, which I’m pretty sure is supposed to be Subjugation instead.
=
Oh hey, I use this Gradient Wipe plugin. It’s pretty handy for animating text boxes.
=
I do think how the game is packaged is very interesting. It’s the entire game, but without any of the usual folders. How did you do that?
Spoiler:
Cons
-
Oh no... you have all of this custom art yet you stuck to default RTP sound effects...
Okay, but in all seriousness, you really need to commit to find more SFX that’s unique to your game since it’s a bit uncanny to see a default light sparkle animation with Bulwark or Lullaby when the game is otherwise so polished.
-
No keyboard rebinding. Please install Yanfly Keyboard Config or have your coder create a custom version that fits your game.
-
Super-not-a-fan of hiding the Options Menu and the Quit Game button inside of the  “Main Menu” section. I know, that sounds weird, but when players press X to access the menu, seeing the Options and Quit selections THERE instead of inside of a submenu feels more natural. (I genuinely thought the options menu didn’t exist because of this, for reference). Likewise, you should have the options menu at the title screen, so players can choose if they want the game to be windowed or not.
-
The forced full screen is very annoying without the ability to toggle it on or off.
-
(
!!
) The game seems quite resource intensive for my laptop. I also saw characters flicker when making new expressions and frames, which tends to happen due to how RPG Maker MV handles multi-frame characters.
-
A typo or two: “What’s luck!” when you get a Life Crystal from the treasure cache should be “What luck!”, removing the “s” since it’s not necessary.
-
So my issue with this combat is that, while you can apply the effects of your little computer faerie friends on top of your normal attack, it’s also very easy to run out of options or get blindsided. For example:
*
You can’t retreat if you know you can’t win (There’s no “run” option)
*
Once a card is used up, you have to find a data cache to get new cards since you’d be out of options otherwise.
*
You can only really hit one enemy at a time, there’s not really any AOE skills.
*
While I do like that the two starter orb enemies die in one hit no matter what, the one that has more HP and can stun you out of the blue is a huge issue.
-
There's also not much tutorialization on how the cards work, nor does it ever really tell you about the "barrier gauge" that nullifies 1 hit for every filled pip you have. That seems like it would reduce confusion on how your game's mechanics work.
Spoiler:
Overall Thoughts
Here's the thing. It's one of the best looking RPG Maker games I've seen come out of anybody who frequents our forum - which is no small feat, given how much effort I've seen people put into their games.
The roguelite deck-building element is very addictive and incentivizes the player to explore and fight however they want, and the base gameplay isn't too complicated. The game also has a ton of cute little moments that made me want to see how our Main Gal (I don't know if she's Margo, so I never call her that) tries to save the world because she's so cute.
But when luck is no longer in your favor, the game spirals out of control almost immediately. I know that's kind of the conceit with these kinds of games, but in this one it stings because you're given just enough to make it feel like when you go down it's your fault.
The awkward placing of the options didn't help much either, since the game starting in full screen and having no way to change it or my keybinds actively hindered me when I was trying to write my thoughts down.
I dunno. All I can say is that I am very excited to see what comes out of this game, because it's clear that there's an incredible amount of love and attention put into it.
